purpose: Fostemsavir is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults who have tried many other HIV medications that are no longer working for them. It is used along with other HIV medicines as part of a combination treatment plan. It is not a cure for HIV, but it helps keep the virus under control and protects your immune system.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking HIV from attaching to and entering your immune cells in the first place. Think of it like putting a lock on the door that HIV tries to use to get inside your cells. By stopping HIV at this very first step, it helps lower the amount of virus in your blood and keeps your immune system stronger.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, headache, feeling tired or weak, trouble sleeping, and dizziness are the most commonly reported side effects. Most of these are mild to moderate and may improve over time.
warnings: This medication can cause serious immune reactions called Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome, where your immune system starts reacting strongly as it recovers. It can also cause changes in heart rhythm (QT prolongation), so tell your doctor if you have heart problems or take other medications that affect your heart. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, as stopping HIV medicines can cause the virus to come back stronger. Some drug interactions can occur, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything you take.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is two 600 mg extended-release tablets taken by mouth twice a day, totaling 1200 mg per day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times every day so you do not miss doses.
